evidence.note: The dominant loop starts here and never really stops: player takes Collar-and-elbow tie-up on 60 of 85 player turns, and the log reads 'The repeated tie-up stalls out - Hall gains escape momentum.'

Turns 37-48 are six identical tie-up/break cycles with zero HP change on either side (health stays [72, 94] the whole way); CPU answers with 'Hall uses the stale tie-up to reset with momentum.' every time.

Hitman's health reaches 1 ('Hall snaps off roundhouse kick - Hitman takes 9 damage.') and then stays at 1 for the remaining 90 turns, so damage stops being a route to resolution and the arc flatlines.
Late match is still the same loop: 'The repeated tie-up stalls out - Hall gains escape momentum.' with health frozen at [1, 48] and player momentum pinned at 0.
Finish is a straight three-count with no kickout beat: 'Referee: 1... / Referee: 2... / Referee: 3! / *** PINFALL - Hall wins ***', near_fall_count 0.

The loop-tax feedback is legible in the menu itself: the tie-up option's note switches from 'enter a tie-up to unlock throws and whips; repeat loops lose steam' to 'tie-up is going stale - pay it off or reset before they steal momentum', and its odds drop to 64%.

Cause and effect are spelled out across two lines: 'The repeated tie-up stalls out - Hall gains escape momentum.' followed on turn 38 by 'Hall uses the stale tie-up to reset with momentum.' A reader can tell exactly what the penalty was.

Curation is honest at the key window: with Hall grounded, the menu leads with 'Finish | Cover - pinfall attempt | pin' and 'Finish | Sharpshooter | 83%'; the policy chose 'Climb to the top rope' instead, so no legal optimal move was hidden.

Status readout misleads: the log says 'Hall snaps off straight right - Hitman takes 7 damage.' but health stays [1, 88], and it stays 1 for the rest of the match. Damage text and the health field disagree with no explanation of the floor.

Groggy is handled as a modifier and read clearly - both options are labeled 'clear the haze before they punish you' ('Shake the cobwebs' 49%, 'Desperation strike' 61%), and the log confirms 'Hitman fights through - the groggy haze lifts!'

stickiness.rematch_reason: The match was a 170-turn stalemate built from one repeated move; after turn 80 the player was locked at 1 HP with 0 momentum and no visible path back, and there was no near-fall or comeback beat to create curiosity about running it again with the same setup.
stickiness.next_experiment: Re-run seed 202 with an aggressive or chaotic policy that actually cashes the grounded windows (e.g. take 'Cover - pinfall attempt' or Sharpshooter at turn 31 instead of climbing), and separately test whether making the tie-up illegal or heavily damage-penalized after two consecutive uses breaks the loop rather than just draining momentum.

evidence.note: The one clear branch point in the whole match - pin and Sharpshooter both offered with Hall grounded at 118 HP - was passed over, and no comparable window reappeared for 139 turns.
By the late match the menu is identical to turn 43's (tie-up 69%, climb, kick, punch, recover), so there is nothing new to discover from continuing.
Match ends on a clean pinfall with near_fall_count 0 and log_uniqueness_ratio 0.28, leaving no cliffhanger.
Real payoff beat exists: 'Hitman snaps off diving elbow drop - Hall takes 24 damage.' off a top-rope setup against a grounded opponent.
Biggest spot of the match lands with a follow-on state line: 'Hall snaps off superplex - Hitman takes 29 damage. / Hitman is rattled - when they're forced up, big payoffs may open.'
Groggy is announced with weight - 'Hitman is GROGGY - power moves and finishers are live!' - but it only fires 3 times in 170 turns (turns 24, 92, 128).
Feedback density collapses under repetition: 'The repeated tie-up stalls out' appears 26 times and 'Hall uses the stale tie-up to reset with momentum.' 24 times, matching log_uniqueness_ratio 0.2796.
The finish has no tension - a straight 1-2-3 with no prior near-fall in the entire match.

top_issues.summary: The loop tax does NOT break the loop. 26 'repeated tie-up stalls out' warnings and 4 'counter is getting predictable' warnings fired, yet the tie-up/break cycle still ran from turn 5 to turn 152 and drove the match to 170 turns. Draining momentum is not a strong enough deterrent when the repeated move remains legal, remains the highest-percentage option in the curated menu (56-69% at turns 43-151), and costs nothing but momentum the player has already lost.
top_issues.suggested_area: game.py loop-tax severity / moves.py legality gating on consecutive repeats

top_issues.summary: Player health floors at 1 from turn 80 through the turn-170 finish - 90 turns in which the log keeps reporting damage ('takes 9 damage', 'takes 7 damage') but the state never changes and the match cannot end by attrition. This is the direct cause of the turn_count gate failure.
top_issues.suggested_area: game.py damage/health resolution and match-end conditions

top_issues.summary: The tax is one-directional and self-reinforcing: every stall hands escape momentum to the opponent, and the CPU cashes it with break_grapple 24 times and grapple_counter 14 times. The punished player ends up at 0 momentum with the same menu, so the feedback tells them they are losing steam without opening an affordable exit.
top_issues.suggested_area: game.py momentum economy / CPU scoring for break_grapple

top_issues.summary: Zero near-falls across 170 turns and a flat three-count finish; the only genuine payoff beats are the turn-33 diving elbow drop and the turn-96 superplex.
